trust_decision.summary: Object keys expanded by permitSetMultiParamEntries become SQL column identifiers and must be escaped as identifiers (backtick doubled) before they are concatenated into SQL text; the decision has to be taken inside every object-expansion encoder, and at the pinned commit the code hand-rolls '`' + key + '`' in three of them.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the SET expansion driven by permitSetMultiParamEntries; this is that branch of the text-protocol parameter encoder and the first hit when grepping the option name.

fix_sites.entry_point: Connection.query(sql, values) / Pool.query over the text protocol, including values nested in an array or reached from the stream-parameter path
Connection.query(sql, values) - the inline duplicate of the parameter encoder inside the COM_QUERY command
fix_sites.module_kind: second_implementation (verbatim copy of TextEncoder.writeParam's object branch)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: escape() only returns a SQL string for the caller and the driver never executes it, and the option's own type docs already call it a source of 'possible injection' when used badly (types/share.d.ts:583-587), so a solver can argue key escaping at that layer is the application's responsibility rather than the connector's.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An existing integration test pins the exact text produced by conn.escape on a SET object: reserved-word and ordinary keys stay quoted identifiers, string values are backslash-escaped, null becomes NULL, a toSqlString object is honoured and function entries are skipped; empty objects still fall back to a JSON string. A reserved-word key must still expand to a column. An over-broad fix that whitelists identifier characters, re-quotes through the public escapeId (which throws on empty and u0000 keys) or re-escapes values breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: plain object as the whole parameter value
object nested as a value inside another expanded object (recursive escapeParameters call)
object inside an array parameter, which is routed to TextEncoder.writeParam
key that is a reserved word and must stay a single quoted identifier
key with no special characters (output must stay unchanged)
empty object, which falls back to a JSON string

O8b_injection_room.sibling: executeSessionVariableQuery builds 'set @@<key>=?' from Object.keys(opts.sessionVariables); a maintainer could have quoted those keys as identifiers exactly like the SET expansion does
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same 'object keys become SQL' intent in the connection layer, already hand-built into SQL, and currently protected only by a character-stripping regex.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an equivalent permitSetMultiParamEntries branch for execute() that wrote object keys as column identifiers
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the documented second transport for parameters; objects are sent as JSON today, so a compatibility branch mirroring the text protocol is a plausible maintainer change and would add a second escapeId site.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a bulk INSERT whose column list is derived from object row keys
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The option's documented use case is 'INSERT ... SET ?', and bulk batching is the natural place to generalise it into a row-object-to-column mapper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a format()/sql-template wrapper composed on Utils.escape that forwards the same expansion
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: escape/escapeId are already the composition point for connections and pools, so a higher-level formatting helper would sit there and inherit the sink.
